requirements.requirement: A Node.js hello-world application runs on node1 in a rootless Podman container under the nodeapp service account.
requirements.summary: The CentOS Stream 10 node is identified directly; the image was built from Node.js 22 with app.js as its command, and live checks before and after reboot show uid 1000 (nodeapp), podman_rootless=true, and the application container running.

requirements.requirement: The container and user service are both named node-hello.
requirements.summary: The Quadlet defines ContainerName=node-hello and generates node-hello.service. Direct pre- and post-reboot observations show that service active and a running container named node-hello.

requirements.requirement: GET / is served over TCP port 8080 with exactly the body Hello, world!.
requirements.summary: Before and after reboot, TCP 8080 listens on 0.0.0.0 and HTTP requests return 200 with exactly 13 bytes; cmp succeeds and the captured body and hex decode precisely to Hello, world! with no trailing newline.

requirements.requirement: The service starts without an interactive nodeapp login.
requirements.summary: A healthy baseline was captured, reboot was scheduled and acknowledged, connection loss observed the bounded disruption, and a different boot ID was then observed. Without any interactive login, the user service, rootless container, listener, and exact HTTP response all recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node1 restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement and observed disruption, independently confirmed boot-ID change, and recovered rootless service, container, listener, and exact application response.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified, so none remained or required reversion. Installing Podman, creating nodeapp with subordinate IDs and lingering, writing the application and Quadlet, building the image, and starting the service were necessary implementation actions. The scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol. Both evidence commands used bounded temporary directories and removed them. Final observations show healthy package state, no failed services, only the required new port-8080 listener, and no executor evidence-file residue; the changed systemd-private /tmp paths are normal reboot-generated replacements.
